newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended firm on Thursday as U.S. October CPI figures in line with expectations induced a flurry of trading and significant curve flattening.
"The whole morning and up to two-thirty, hardly anything was going on... but this afternoon there were lots of trades across the curve," one trader said.
July 6.25 percent 1998 bonds were the pick of the crop, with trading volume reaching about a billion guilders.
However, the rise in activity in the short end did not lead to price gains as investors continued to regard the yields as unattractive.
"There's quite an incentive to sell (the short-term)," one trader said.
While all maturities gained, the curve flattened noticeably. Jan 2023s were up 0.41 points. July 6.25 1998s only added 0.03.
January 2006s, meanwhile, were up 0.18, but the paper suffered slightly against bunds, the spread narrowing one basis point to -7 bp.

Traders said the morning's 2006 issue from ABN AMRO, increased from 500 million to 600 million guilders within half an hour of issue, led to some switching from Jan 2006s and some hedging to the detriment of the state paper.
"(The ABN issue) put pressure on that sector and therefore the spread is less wide," one trader said.
